items.title: Even ICE Thinks Smart Glasses Are a Privacy Liability
items.excerpt: ICE has banned its employees from wearing smart glasses, warning the devices could "unintentionally capture, record or transmit sensitive information." When even a surveillance agency bans always-on camera eyewear, the social-acceptability problem designers keep waving away becomes a hard product constraint.

items.title: Eufy's Latest Security System Is an All-Seeing, Local-First Camera Array
items.excerpt: Anker's Eufy unveiled the NVR E50, a hardwired system that runs on-device AI processing with NAS-style local storage, starting at $1,200 for up to eight dual-lens PTZ cameras and 16TB of local recording. It is a bet that home AI vision sells better as local hardware you own than as a cloud subscription.

items.title: Millions of Comcast WiFi Routers Can Now Tell When You're Moving Around the House
items.excerpt: Comcast is rolling out Xfinity Shield with WiFi Motion, turning ordinary routers into whole-home presence sensors with no new hardware and no camera. Sensing is quietly migrating into infrastructure people never chose as a sensor, which reframes what ambient-AI interfaces have to disclose.

items.title: DeepMind's newest model allows Pixel 11 devices to transcribe sign language into text
items.excerpt: DeepMind's SL2T model ships on the Pixel 11 family, letting deaf and hard-of-hearing users sign directly at the phone to search, message and talk to Gemini, starting with ASL-to-English. On-device AI is turning the camera into an accessibility input method, not just a photo tool.

items.title: Amazon's Alexa+ AI assistant is now free for anyone with a Fire TV device
items.excerpt: Amazon dropped the $20/month fee and is giving Alexa+ free to every US Fire TV owner, pushing conversational, context-aware assistance onto the living-room screen at once. The TV becomes the default surface for agentic voice UI, and remote-plus-voice navigation design is suddenly a mass-market problem.

items.title: A robot could eventually conduct your blood draw at the doctor's office
items.excerpt: The FDA cleared Aletta, a robotic device that finds veins with infrared and ultrasound, then inserts the needle and bandages the arm while a phlebotomist supervises. Designing trust and hand-off cues for a machine that touches your body is now a shipping product problem, not a concept study.

items.title: Google could soon make it easier to ask Gemini to take a look at things
items.excerpt: An APK teardown shows Google building an accessibility shortcut for Guided Vision that drops users straight into Gemini Live's camera mode via a double volume-button hold or a floating icon. The hardware button is being redesigned as the fastest path to a multimodal assistant.

items.title: First look: Gemini could soon remember details from your screenshots with one tap
items.excerpt: A share-sheet action in development would let users push details from any image straight into Gemini's memory with a single tap, no typing or app-hopping. Memory capture is being pushed into the OS share sheet, which changes how much of a phone's UI is a front end for the assistant.

items.title: Apple's Upcoming Home Hub to Feature Widget Gallery
items.excerpt: Apple's delayed smart display will ship a Widget Gallery that pulls first- and third-party iPhone widgets onto the hub's screen with smart rotation. The company is answering the ambient-display question with editable widgets rather than a pure conversational surface — a real fork in smart-home UI design.

items.title: Next Apple TV Rumored to Get Five New Features, Including Siri AI
items.excerpt: The next Apple TV 4K is expected to jump to an A17 Pro-class chip with more RAM specifically to run Apple Intelligence, plus an N1 Wi-Fi 7 chip and a redesigned Siri Remote. Set-top boxes are being re-specced around on-device assistants, and the remote is being redrawn to match.

items.title: Apple Accidentally Leaked More Than 10 New Products in macOS Update
items.excerpt: Code in the macOS 26.7 release candidate names over ten unreleased devices, including camera-equipped AirPods, a foldable iPhone, a smart home hub and a new Apple TV with an updated Siri Remote. It is an unusually complete map of where Apple thinks AI hardware form factors are going next.

items.title: Pixel Watch 5 initial review: The 41mm finally worth buying
items.excerpt: The Pixel Watch 5 leans on software: an At a Glance surface for real-time info and gestures that make the watch mostly touch-free, while updated ML models make sleep tracking 15% more accurate. Blood pressure sensing arrives in September, so the AI story is now sensing accuracy rather than screen decoration.

items.title: Pixel 11 Pro initial review: Gemini Intelligence is the highlight, not HiLight
items.excerpt: The review argues the Pixel 11 Pro's real upgrade is Gemini Intelligence — Proactive Assistance and a rebuilt voice transcription tool — rather than the new camera hardware. A flagship phone is being reviewed primarily on assistant UX and accessibility controls, which is where the craft work now sits.

items.title: macOS Golden Gate adds a new app to your Mac; here's what it can do
items.excerpt: macOS 27 introduces a standalone Siri app for the Mac — a first — with persistent conversation history and iCloud sync across devices. The assistant graduates from an invisible overlay to a real window with navigation, history and state that has to be designed like any other app.

items.title: Google Assistant is dead, and I won't miss it thanks to my local LLM
items.excerpt: With Google Assistant shutting down on September 4, 2026, the writer replaced it with a local language model running on the phone itself rather than accepting the Gemini chatbot as a successor. On-device models are becoming a consumer-level opt-out from cloud assistants, latency and privacy included.

items.title: A $200 device replaced my phone's biggest job, and now I record meetings without killing the battery
items.excerpt: The Comu Action Pro is a $200 dedicated AI recorder with six adaptive mics, a magnetic phone mount and about 70 hours of battery that auto-transfers and transcribes what it captures. It is the strongest argument yet that single-purpose AI hardware beats a phone app when the job is capture-and-transcribe.

items.title: Someone made a Raspberry Pi D&D DM cyberdeck that tracks campaigns, rolls dice, and generates NPCs
items.excerpt: A 14-year-old built a Raspberry Pi 5 cyberdeck running LoreKeeper, which generates NPCs, rolls dice, tracks campaigns and syncs with D&D Beyond using onboard AI. A reminder that the most convincing AI gadget design right now is purpose-built, tactile and made by one person.

items.title: Code leak: Apple HomePad to come in two versions with features borrowed from Apple Watch
items.excerpt: macOS 26.7 beta code describes Apple's HomePad as a near-square 7-inch touchscreen shipping in two variants, with customizable faces lifted straight from the Apple Watch. Apple is porting watch-face design language onto a wall-mounted ambient AI display, which sets the visual grammar for the whole category.
